formats.key: claim(address _rewardOwner, address _recipient, uint24 _rewardEpochId, bool _wrap, (bytes32[] merkleProof, (uint24 rewardEpochId, bytes20 beneficiary, uint120 amount, uint8 claimType) body)[] _proofs)
effects: The contract pays the reward owner's DIRECT and FEE proof amounts to _recipient. For FEE proofs it first burns a share set by the burn factor that FlareSystemsCalculator returns.

It also pays the owner's weight-based rewards (WSGB delegation, mirrored stake, C-chain stake) for every unclaimed epoch up to _rewardEpochId. Proofs do not carry these amounts: the contract computes them from storage.
The payout goes to _recipient as native SGB, or as WSGB through wNat.depositTo when _wrap is true.
The contract marks all of the owner's epochs up to _rewardEpochId as claimed, so they cannot be claimed again.
Weight-based proofs initialise reward pools for any beneficiary, which is a state change only.
Nothing leaves the signer. The function is not payable.
formats.shown: "Claim rewards to {recipient}", with the reward owner, the recipient, the last epoch, SGB or WSGB, and a list of proof beneficiaries, proof amounts and claim types.

findings.title: claim: 'Proof amount' looks like the payout, but it is not what the recipient receives.
findings.evidence: RewardManager.sol _claim: `_rewardAmountWei += _claimWeightBasedRewards(_rewardOwner, _recipient, _rewardEpochId, ...)`. _claimRewards pays `unclaimedRewardAmount.mulDiv(_rewardWeight, unclaimedRewardWeight)`, which is a share of the pool. Descriptor: label 'Proof amount' on `#._proofs.[].body.amount`. Case 1 shows '5 SGB' with 'WSGB delegation', but that number is the total of the pool, not the signer's share. Case 3 has no proofs and shows no amount, yet the call still pays rewards for every epoch up to 303.
findings.fix: Rename the field to 'Reward pool total (proof)'. Change the intent to 'Claim all rewards up to epoch' so the signer does not read the proof amounts as the payout.

findings.title: claim: a Provider fee proof shows the full amount, but the contract burns part of it.
findings.evidence: RewardManager.sol _claimFromDirectOrFeeClaim: `if (rewardClaim.claimType == ClaimType.FEE) { ... _burnAmountWei = ...mulDiv(burnFactor, PPM_MAX) ...; _rewardAmountWei -= _burnAmountWei;` Case 2 shows 'Proof amount 3 SGB' with 'Claim Type Provider fee'.
findings.fix: Label FEE amounts 'Up to', or add a note that part of a provider fee can be burned.

findings.title: claim: proof amounts show SGB while 'Receive as' WSGB means the payout is wrapped.
findings.evidence: RewardManager.sol _transferOrWrap: `if (_wrap) { wNat.depositTo{value: _rewardAmount}(_recipient); }`. Case 1 shows 'Receive as WSGB' next to 'Proof amount 5 SGB'.
findings.fix: Add the token to the interpolated intent: 'Claim rewards as {_wrap} to {_recipient}'.

findings.title: claim: the beneficiary, amount and type of each proof show as separate lists that the signer cannot pair.
findings.evidence: Case 2 shows 'Proof beneficiary', 'Proof beneficiary', 'Proof amount 3 SGB', 'Proof amount 7 SGB', 'Claim Type Provider fee', 'Claim Type Mirrored stake'.
findings.fix: Put the three proof fields in one field group on `#._proofs.[]` so each proof shows as one row.

findings.title: claim: the total payout depends on storage, so no descriptor can show it.
findings.evidence: RewardManager.sol _claimWNatRewards / _claimMirrorRewards / _claimCChainRewards read wNat.balanceOfAt, delegatesOfAt, pChainStakeMirror.stakesOfAt and cChainStake.stakesOfAt at the vote power block.

findings.title: claim: the epoch of each proof is hidden and can differ from the epoch shown.
findings.evidence: Descriptor: 'Proofs Body Epoch Id' has `visible: never`. _processProofs only checks `_proofs[i].body.rewardEpochId >= _minClaimableEpochId`.

formats.key: claimProxy(address _msgSender, address _rewardOwner, address _recipient, uint24 _rewardEpochId, bool _wrap, (bytes32[] merkleProof, (uint24 rewardEpochId, bytes20 beneficiary, uint120 amount, uint8 claimType) body)[] _proofs)
effects: Only the FtsoRewardManager proxy contract can call this function. A transaction a person signs and sends to this address reverts.
When the proxy calls it, the effects are the same as claim: proof and weight-based rewards for the owner up to _rewardEpochId go to _recipient, as SGB or as WSGB; FEE proofs are partly burned.
Nothing leaves the signer. The function is not payable.
formats.shown: "Claim rewards to {recipient}" with the caller, the reward owner, the recipient, the last epoch, SGB or WSGB, and the proof lists.

findings.title: claimProxy only accepts calls from the FtsoRewardManager contract, so no signer can call it directly.
findings.evidence: RewardManager.sol claimProxy: `require(msg.sender == ftsoRewardManagerProxy, "only ftso reward manager proxy");`. Case 4 ('Claim through the legacy FtsoRewardManager') sends the transaction straight to 0xe26a…b9a7, so it reverts.
findings.fix: Remove this format, or bind it to the FtsoRewardManager deployment that forwards the call.

findings.title: claimProxy: 'Proof amount' looks like the payout, but it is a pool total or a pre-burn amount.
findings.evidence: Same code as claim (_claim → _claimWeightBasedRewards, and the FEE burn in _claimFromDirectOrFeeClaim). Descriptor label 'Proof amount'. Case 4 shows '12 SGB' with 'C-chain stake'.
findings.fix: Rename the field to 'Reward pool total (proof)'.

findings.title: claimProxy: proof fields show as separate parallel lists that the signer cannot pair.
findings.fix: Put them in one field group on `#._proofs.[]`.

findings.title: claimProxy test case 4 sends a transaction directly that the contract always rejects.
findings.evidence: Case 4: `to` is 0xe26ad68b…b9a7 with selector 0xaa145443. claimProxy requires msg.sender == ftsoRewardManagerProxy.
findings.fix: Make the test the FtsoRewardManager call that forwards to claimProxy, or drop the format.

formats.key: initialiseWeightBasedClaims((bytes32[] merkleProof, (uint24 rewardEpochId, bytes20 beneficiary, uint120 amount, uint8 claimType) body)[] _proofs)
effects: For each weight-based proof (WSGB delegation, mirrored stake, C-chain stake) with a valid merkle proof, the contract records the beneficiary's reward pool amount and vote power for that epoch.
DIRECT and FEE proofs are skipped and pay nothing.
No funds move to or from the signer. Anyone can call it.
formats.shown: "Initialise claims for {beneficiary}" with the beneficiary, the proof amount and the claim type of each proof.

findings.title: initialiseWeightBasedClaims shows 'Proof amount' in SGB, but no funds move.
findings.evidence: RewardManager.sol initialiseWeightBasedClaims calls `_processProofs(address(0), address(0), _proofs, ...)`, which only writes `state.amount` and `state.weight`. Case 6 shows 'Proof amount 8 SGB'.
findings.fix: Change the intent to 'Register reward pools (no payout)'. Rename the field to 'Pool total'.

findings.title: initialiseWeightBasedClaims: DIRECT and FEE proofs show as if processed, but the contract ignores them.
findings.evidence: RewardManager.sol _processProofs: `if (claimType == ClaimType.DIRECT || claimType == ClaimType.FEE) { if (_rewardOwner != address(0)) {...} }`. _rewardOwner is address(0) here. The 'Claim Type' enum lists 'Direct' and 'Provider fee'.
findings.fix: Add a note that only stake-weighted claim types are initialised.

findings.title: initialiseWeightBasedClaims: proof fields show as separate lists that the signer cannot pair.
findings.fix: Put them in one field group on `#._proofs.[]`.

formats.key: autoClaim(address[] _rewardOwners, uint24 _rewardEpochId, (bytes32[] merkleProof, (uint24 rewardEpochId, bytes20 beneficiary, uint120 amount, uint8 claimType) body)[] _proofs)
effects: The signer is the claim executor. The contract sends the signer executorFee × number of owners in native SGB.

For each owner, the contract claims weight-based rewards up to _rewardEpochId, and PDA rewards when a PDA is set. It wraps the rewards minus the executor fee and sends them as WSGB to the claim address (the owner's PDA or the owner).
Weight-based proofs are initialised. DIRECT and FEE proofs are ignored and pay nothing.
All owners' epochs up to _rewardEpochId are marked as claimed.
formats.shown: "Auto-claim and wrap rewards for {owners}" with the reward owners, the last epoch and the proof lists.

findings.title: autoClaim does not say that the signer receives an executor fee in SGB for each owner.
findings.evidence: RewardManager.sol autoClaim: `_transferOrWrap(msg.sender, executorFeeValue * _rewardOwners.length, false);`. The intent is 'Auto-claim and wrap rewards'. No field mentions a fee.
findings.fix: Change the intent to 'Auto-claim rewards, earn executor fee'. The fee amount is in storage, so it cannot be a field.

findings.title: autoClaim says 'for {owners}', but rewards go to each owner's PDA when one is set.
findings.evidence: RewardManager.sol autoClaim: `_transferOrWrap(claimAddress, rewardAmount, true);` where claimAddresses come from claimSetupManager.getAutoClaimAddressesAndExecutorFee. Interpolated intent: 'Auto-claim and wrap rewards for {_rewardOwners.[]}'.
findings.fix: Add a note: 'Rewards go to each owner's personal delegation account if set'.

findings.title: autoClaim: 'Proof amount' is a pool total, and DIRECT and FEE proofs pay nothing.
findings.evidence: autoClaim calls `_processProofs(address(0), address(0), _proofs, ...)`: initialise only. Case 5 shows 'Proof amount 25 SGB'.

findings.title: autoClaim: proof fields show as separate parallel lists.
findings.fix: Put them in one field group on `#._proofs.[]`.

findings.title: autoClaim: the fee and the claim addresses come from ClaimSetupManager storage, so no descriptor can show them.

couldNotCheck: ClaimSetupManager (getAutoClaimAddressesAndExecutorFee) is not in the directory. It sets the executor fee the signer receives in autoClaim and the claim addresses that receive the owners' rewards.
